Years ago, MacBooks had slots that allowed you to lock the device to a table leg or similar object with a cable lock. These slots were most useful in coffee shops—when you wanted to go back to the counter to order another drink but didn't want to carry your laptop along.

Those slots have long disappeared, but now you can buy adapters to lock down a MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro……

To remember those anti-theft slots on the side of the machine, you have to be a fairly seasoned MacBook user. These slots were designed for T-shaped accessories: insert the accessory into the slot, rotate it 90 degrees, then lock it in place. The most common design was a cable loop that could be threaded through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived this concept, launching adapters that can be installed on the corners or edges of a MacBook to attach a cable lock. These adapters use a two-piece construction, clamping onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version to its existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It must be emphasised that these locks have always been very low-level protection devices, intended only to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and walking away in a matter of seconds. I've personally used one in smaller coffee shops, where I could still see my table when going to the counter for another tea, but I would never rely on a lock alone to let my MacBook out of my sight.

These adapters cost $70, which isn't cheap, since you still need to buy a lock separately; but if you happen to have an old lock lying in a drawer, it might be worth bringing it back into service.
